name: terminal
description: Execute a shell command and capture stdout/stderr. Use for running tests, build scripts, system commands.

manual.overview: Use terminal to execute any shell command: run scripts, install packages, manage processes, compile code. This is the most powerful tool — use it responsibly.
tips: Always set cwd when running project-specific commands to avoid path issues.
Use timeout for commands that might hang (network calls, build scripts).
Chain commands with && for sequential execution: 'cd /app && npm install && npm test'.
Prefer specific tools (git, file_read) over terminal equivalents when available — they are safer and more structured.
edge_cases: Interactive commands (vim, less, python REPL) will hang — avoid them.
Commands requiring user input (password prompts, y/n confirmations) will timeout.
Stderr is captured alongside stdout — check for error messages in the output.
Long-running commands will be killed after the timeout.
